cells.tense: You can see the whole shape of a thing and still let it keep becoming.
cells.act: feel it alongside them and keep your own side
cells.ask: Go through one hard hour with someone you're helping and feel what they're feeling without dropping what you're feeling. Their fear stays theirs. Your hour stays yours. Hold both for the length of it.
cells.core:
You're tending something young — a person, a project, a thing still taking shape — and from where you stand you can see the whole of it: what it needs, what it will become. That is rarer than it sounds. What keeps it kind is that nothing has been closed off. You're still watching for what you haven't seen yet, and sometimes it arrives.

On the good days your own life runs alongside theirs in the same hour. Their dread doesn't become your dread; their pride isn't something you did. That's the gap between standing with someone and dissolving into them. Pick one hard hour with the thing you're tending and stay on your own side of it — feel what's happening for them and keep what's happening for you. Two whole people, no merging.

cells.tense: You'll have decided how this turns out before it's had a chance to turn.
cells.act: refuse the second thing so the first can have you
cells.ask: Think of what you're tending that most needs you now. When something smaller pulls — a message, a task, a fire that can burn a while — leave it. No deadline. Just the first thing, and the second left where it is.
cells.core:
There's a thing you're tending, and your read on it has run ahead of it. You know what it needs, what it will be, what's wrong with it — that's usually useful. Lately it lands as verdict. The person can feel the difference: being read and filed instead of watched. What they came to you for was room to grow into, and what's in the space instead is a scoreboard.

Something you're growing needs you undecided. Let it stay that way. When the verdict starts forming in your chest, leave it unspoken and go do the next real thing with what you're tending — the smaller pull can keep waiting. This isn't softening. You're letting a future that hasn't happened keep its options.

cells.tense: You stood at that door a long time, and you're still standing where it used to be.
cells.act: open the thing you have been assuming you knew and look at it unlabelled
cells.ask: There's something you're tending that has a label on it in your mind. Set the label aside and stay with it ten minutes as though it were new — no fixing, no filing, no fitting it to the plan. Hear what it says that you hadn't counted on.
cells.core:
You can see the pattern. You've watched this shape come around enough that looking again feels like work you've already done. New things arrive and get sorted into what you've seen before, quickly, before they can get a word in. You'd say you're still searching. From where anyone else stands, the search happens mostly in your head and nothing lands.

There's something you're tending that has already got a name in your mind. This week, set the name down and spend ten minutes with it as though it were fresh — no fixing, no filing, no working out what it means for the plan. Stay nearby and let it speak something you hadn't reckoned on. Ten minutes. Then you can take the name back, or not.

cells.tense: You are already seeing the pattern here and won't take credit for the seeing.
cells.act: adjust the share until it is fair, then stop
cells.ask: Notice the next time you give more than you get back with someone you're helping. Change one thing about the share so it sits closer to even, once. Then leave the rest alone.
cells.core:
You're tending something young — a person, a start, a thing just beginning — and the shape it's headed toward is already in view for you. Ask how you know and you'd say you're just paying attention to what's there. The read arrived before you noticed you were the one reading. A hand is on this, and it isn't signing its name.

That matters because the exchange between you and the person you're helping has gone uneven and you haven't said so. Maybe you're giving more than you take back, maybe less. Next time something passes between you, change one thing so the share sits closer to even — a shift in what you give, or in what you let them give you. One adjustment, and then no returning to it.
